meta.title: Maya Fernandes | Customer Success Leader
meta.description: Maya Fernandes: customer success leader, onboarding architect and data-minded operator with 11 years in B2B SaaS.

hero.intro: Eleven years in B2B SaaS, from answering support tickets to leading a 30-person customer success organisation. I design onboarding that sticks, build teams that own the customer outcome, and use data to see churn before it happens.

leadership.headline: The best retention strategy is a [[customer who succeeds early.]] I build teams and processes around that one idea.
leadership.lede: Support agent, onboarding specialist, CSM, team lead and head of CS. These principles have carried through every role.

pillars.title: Early value
pillars.text: If a customer hasn't seen value in 30 days, nothing else we do matters much.

pillars.title: Signals over hunches
pillars.text: Health scores, usage data and renewal risk reviewed every week, not every quarter.

pillars.title: Owners, not ticket-takers
pillars.text: Every CSM owns a book of business and the outcome that comes with it.

pillars.title: One team with Sales
pillars.text: Shared accounts, shared forecasts and no hand-off cliff after the contract is signed.

work.lede: Three projects, each showing a different side of how I work. Keep scrolling, they stack.

cases.where: As Head of Customer Success, Northwind, 2022 to present
cases.title: Rebuilding onboarding from scratch
cases.problem: New customers took two months to see value, and a third of first-year churn started in onboarding.
cases.action: Redesigned onboarding into a 21-day guided programme with milestones, in-app checklists and a dedicated launch CSM.
cases.result: Time-to-value fell from 60 to 21 days and first-year churn dropped by a quarter.

cases.where: As CS Operations Lead, Northwind, 2020 to 2022
cases.title: A health score that actually predicts churn
cases.problem: The team found out about churn at renewal time, when it was too late.
cases.action: Built a health score from product usage, support volume and sentiment, and a weekly risk review around it.
cases.result: At-risk accounts flagged an average of 90 days earlier; save rate on flagged accounts doubled.

cases.title: Scaling the team without losing the culture
cases.problem: Rapid hiring was diluting quality and new CSMs took months to ramp.
cases.action: Created a CSM career path, a four-week ramp programme and peer coaching circles.
cases.result: Ramp time halved and team engagement stayed above 85% through 3x growth.

career.title: From the support queue to head of CS
career.lede: Support, onboarding, account management and leadership across three companies. Open any role for the detail.

roles.title: Head of Customer Success

highlights: Grew net revenue retention from 104% to 118% in two years.
Redesigned onboarding, cutting time-to-value from 60 to 21 days.
Built the CS career path and promoted six people into team-lead roles.

roles.title: CS Operations Lead
roles.summary: Set up CS operations: tooling, health scoring and reporting.
highlights: Built the customer health score and weekly risk review.
Migrated the team to a single CS platform and automated renewal workflows.

roles.title: Customer Success Team Lead
roles.summary: Led a team of CSMs managing mid-market accounts.
highlights: Scaled the team from 4 to 12 CSMs while keeping engagement above 85%.
Created the four-week CSM ramp programme.

roles.title: Support Specialist
roles.growth: Support to team lead in two years
roles.summary: Where it started: frontline technical support for SMB customers.
highlights: Top CSAT on the team for six consecutive quarters.
Wrote the first internal knowledge base for the support team.
